g.text: Accumulated. Five years of treatment recovers only about half the

text.style: font-size: 8.3px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #2d6282

g.text: predicted coronary benefit: 14% fewer coronary events.

g.text: Immediate. The same five years delivers

text.style: font-size: 8.3px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #b24a45

g.text: essentially all of the predicted stroke

font-size: 8.2px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #626a73

g.text: The asymmetry is the signature of the mechanism: the 1990 overview of antihypertensive trials (Collins et al.) cashed in all of pressure’s

text.style: font-size: 8.2px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #626a73

g.text: stroke benefit in five years and half of its coronary benefit, because routes 1–3 are written into thirty years of accumulated plaque.
